newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner shifts Eurobond responsibility to London.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner shifts Eurobond responsibility to London.

text.p: Germany's second largest commercial bank, Dresdner Bank AG, said on Tuesday it was shifting responsibility for its eurobond business to London in a bid to drum up additional business in other currencies.

Leonhard Fischer, joint head of the bank's Global Markets Division, told Reuters that the bank was buying in a team of 16 or 17 eurobond experts by taking over London-based Luthy Baillie Dowsett & Pethick Ltd.
Fischer thereby confirmed a report carried in today's Berosen-Zeitung business newspaper.

Fischer, who termed the newspaper report "factually correct" confirmed that Peter Luthy would take over global responsibility for Dresdner's Eurobond business in all major currencies. Luthy himself would report to Frankfurt, he said.
"There will be no physical movement of business to Frankfurt," he added, making clear that responsibility for domestic issues and government bonds would remain in Frankfurt.
He added that the main aim of the move was to increase Dresdner's business in issues denominated in major currencies other than marks.
"Dresdner has so far been primarily a mark issuance address," Fischer said.
The takeover of LBDP, which has specialist experience in eurobonds and in credit spread business, had yet to be finalised, he added.
